name: different-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group
description: A standard schema version in a merge group must match the withStandard partner of the group's library schemas.
explanation: All schemas in a merge group (the unprefixed schemas, or the schemas sharing one namespace prefix) must resolve to a single standard schema partner. Here testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.5.0 (its withStandard attribute), but the group also lists standard schema 8.4.0. A standard schema in a merge group must be the same version as the group partner, so the load fails.
common_causes: Listing a standard schema version different from the library's withStandard partner
Updating the library schema version without updating the standard schema version in the specification
Copying a version specification from a dataset that used an older library release
Not knowing which standard version a library schema is partnered with
correction_strategy: Look up the library schema's withStandard partner and either list that standard version or omit the standard schema entirely, since the partner is included automatically.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.0.0 has withStandard=8.5.0, so the standard schema in its merge group must be 8.5.0.
A partnered library schema automatically includes its standard schema partner, so the standard version can simply be omitted.

correction_patterns: Check the withStandard attribute in the library schema header
Set the standard schema version in the group to the withStandard value
Or remove the standard schema from the list and rely on the partner
fix_instructions: 1. Find the withStandard value of each library schema in the merge group
2. Confirm all libraries in the group have the same withStandard value
3. Change the listed standard schema version to that value, or delete it
4. Reload and confirm the schemas load without error
validation_hints: The withStandard attribute is in the library schema's XML header
A partnered library loads its standard partner automatically
Schema loading happens before any annotation is validated

name: extra-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group
description: A standard schema in a merge group is allowed when it matches the group partner and adds nothing to the merged result.
explanation: This combination loads. testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.5.0, and the listed standard schema 8.5.0 matches the group partner, so it is allowed and adds nothing to the merged result.
common_causes: Believing that listing the standard schema alongside its partnered library is an error
correction_strategy: No correction needed; a standard schema matching the group partner is allowed and adds nothing to the merged result, though it can simply be omitted.

correction_examples.explanation: A standard schema listed with a partnered library must match the library's withStandard partner (8.5.0); it then adds nothing to the merged result.

name: standard-schema-after-library-loads
description: A standard schema matching the group partner may appear anywhere in the list; schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order.
explanation: This combination loads. Schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order, so this is the same merge group as extra-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group with the standard schema listed after the library instead of before it. The standard schema 8.5.0 matches the partner of testconflict_2.0.0, so it is allowed and adds nothing to the merged result.
common_causes: Believing that the standard schema must be listed before its partnered library schemas
correction_strategy: No correction needed; the position of a standard schema in the list does not affect whether the merge group loads.

correction_examples.explanation: Order is irrelevant; what matters is that the listed standard schema matches the library's withStandard partner (8.5.0).

name: standard-schema-after-library-mismatch
description: A standard schema that differs from the group partner fails wherever it appears in the list; schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order, so this is the same merge group as different-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group with the standard schema listed after the library instead of before it. testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.5.0, and the listed standard schema 8.4.0 differs from the group partner, so the load fails regardless of order.
common_causes: Expecting a later standard schema in the list to be overridden by an earlier library schema's partner
Listing an outdated standard schema version after upgrading a partnered library
correction_strategy: Change the standard schema version to match the library's withStandard partner, remove it, or give it its own namespace prefix. Reordering the list does not help.

correction_examples.explanation: The standard schema now matches the partner of testconflict_2.0.0.
Under a namespace prefix the standard schema 8.4.0 forms its own merge group and no longer conflicts.

name: same-library-two-versions-in-group
description: Two different versions of the same library schema cannot appear in the same merge group.
explanation: Different versions of the same schema cannot appear in the same merge group. testconflict_2.0.0 and testconflict_2.1.0 are both partnered with standard schema 8.5.0 and 2.1.0 is 2.0.0 plus one added tag (Object-four), so no element conflict is involved; the load fails because two versions of one library are listed in the same merge group.
common_causes: Believing that two versions of one library merge when their elements do not conflict
Concatenating version lists that name different versions of the same library
correction_strategy: Use a single version of the library, or give the second version its own namespace so the two versions are in different merge groups.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.1.0 contains everything in testconflict_2.0.0, so one version suffices.
With its own namespace the second version is in a separate merge group, so the version rule does not apply.

name: prefixed-standard-schema-forms-own-group
description: A standard schema under a namespace prefix forms its own merge group independent of the unprefixed group.
explanation: This combination loads. The unprefixed group holds standard schema 8.5.0 and the sc: group holds standard schema 8.4.0. Each namespace is a separate merge group, so the two standard versions do not conflict.
common_causes: Believing only library schemas may appear under a namespace prefix
Believing all standard schema versions in a specification must agree
correction_strategy: No correction needed; use a namespace prefix to load a second standard schema version alongside the default one.

correction_examples.explanation: Two bare standard versions share the unprefixed group and fail; prefixing the second gives it its own merge group.

name: incompatible-merge-schemas
description: Library schemas in a merge group must all have the same standard schema partner.
explanation: Partnered library schemas can only merge into one namespace if they share the same withStandard partner. testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.5.0 while testminimal_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.4.0, so these two libraries cannot form a merge group and the load fails.
common_causes: Combining library schema versions released against different standard schema versions
Upgrading one library in a specification without upgrading the others
Assuming any versions of two libraries can be combined
correction_strategy: Choose library schema versions that share the same withStandard partner, or put the incompatible library in its own namespace with a prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.0.0 and testminimal_2.1.0 are both partnered with standard schema 8.5.0, so they can merge.
Giving testminimal_2.0.0 its own namespace prefix removes it from the unprefixed merge group, so the partners no longer need to match.

name: multiple-libraries-with-same-partner
description: Several library schemas with the same standard schema partner merge into one namespace.
explanation: This combination loads. testconflict_2.1.0, testclash_1.0.0, and testminimal_2.1.0 are all partnered with standard schema 8.5.0, and their library elements are either disjoint or identical (Shared-item appears in testconflict and testclash as identical copies), so all three merge with their shared partner into a single unprefixed vocabulary.
common_causes: Believing that at most two schemas can be combined
Believing that library schemas always require namespace prefixes
correction_strategy: No correction needed; any number of partnered libraries sharing the same withStandard partner can merge if their elements do not conflict.

correction_examples.explanation: testminimal_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.4.0 and would break the group; testminimal_2.1.0 shares the 8.5.0 partner with the other two libraries.

name: merge-order-independent-loads
description: Reordering the schemas of a loadable merge group does not change the result; schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order.
explanation: This combination loads. It lists the same three libraries as multiple-libraries-with-same-partner in reverse order. Schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order, so the merged vocabulary is the same: all three are partnered with 8.5.0 and their elements are either disjoint or identical.
common_causes: Believing that library schemas must be listed in a particular order to merge
correction_strategy: No correction needed; the order in which the schemas of a merge group are listed does not affect the merged result.

correction_examples.explanation: testminimal_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.4.0 and would fail in any position; testminimal_2.1.0 shares the 8.5.0 partner.

name: partnered-library-alone-loads-with-partner
description: A partnered library schema listed alone automatically includes its standard schema partner.
explanation: This specification loads. A partnered library schema is distributed merged with its standard schema partner, so listing testconflict_2.0.0 alone provides both the testconflict library tags and the standard schema 8.5.0 tags. Standard schema tags such as Red validate without the standard schema being listed.
common_causes: Believing the standard schema must always be listed explicitly
Believing standard tags are unavailable when only a library schema is specified
correction_strategy: No correction needed; a partnered library schema alone supplies its standard schema partner.

correction_examples.explanation: Listing a non-matching standard schema (8.4.0) with testconflict_2.0.0 (partnered with 8.5.0) fails; the library alone already includes its partner.

name: namespaced-groups-load-independently
description: Schemas with different namespace prefixes form independent merge groups whose partners need not match.
explanation: This combination loads. Each namespace prefix forms its own merge group: the unprefixed group holds standard schema 8.4.0, the sc: group holds testconflict_2.1.0 (with its 8.5.0 partner), and the ts: group holds the unpartnered testminimal_1.0.0, which is allowed because it is alone in its own namespace. Compatibility rules apply within each group separately, so the differing standard versions across groups are not a conflict.
common_causes: Believing all schemas in a specification must share one standard schema version
Believing unpartnered library schemas can no longer be used at all
correction_strategy: No correction needed; use namespace prefixes to combine schemas whose partners differ or that are unpartnered.

correction_examples.explanation: Unprefixed, testconflict_2.1.0's 8.5.0 partner conflicts with 8.4.0 and unpartnered testminimal_1.0.0 cannot share a namespace; prefixes give each schema its own merge group.

name: two-standard-versions-in-same-merge-group
description: Two different standard schema versions cannot appear in the same merge group.
explanation: A merge group resolves to exactly one standard schema partner. Listing two different bare standard schema versions in the unprefixed group gives the group two conflicting partners, so the load fails.
common_causes: Concatenating version specifications from two datasets
Trying to validate against two standard versions at once
Leaving the old standard version in place when upgrading
correction_strategy: Keep a single standard schema version per namespace; use a namespace prefix if a second standard version is genuinely needed.

correction_examples.explanation: Choose the one standard version the annotations should validate against.
If both versions are needed, put the second in its own namespace and prefix its tags with old: in annotations.

name: unpartnered-library-in-shared-namespace
description: An unpartnered library schema cannot share a namespace with other schemas.
explanation: Unpartnered library schemas (no withStandard attribute) must be in their own namespace. testconflict_1.1.0 is unpartnered, so it cannot be merged into the unprefixed group with standard schema 8.5.0, and the load fails.
common_causes: Using an old unpartnered library release where a partnered version now exists
Omitting the namespace prefix an unpartnered library requires
Assuming all library schema versions behave like partnered ones
correction_strategy: Either upgrade to a partnered version of the library or give the unpartnered library its own namespace prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.5.0, so it merges into the unprefixed group.
The prefix gives the unpartnered library its own namespace; its tags are then written with the tc: prefix.

name: two-unpartnered-libraries-in-same-namespace
description: Two unpartnered library schemas cannot share one namespace prefix.
explanation: Schemas with the same namespace prefix form one merge group, and merging requires partnered schemas with a shared standard partner. testconflict_1.1.2 and testminimal_1.0.0 are both unpartnered, so they cannot merge, and an unpartnered schema must be alone in its namespace. The load fails.
common_causes: Reusing one prefix for several old-style library schemas
Assuming a prefix is a label rather than a merge group identifier
correction_strategy: Give each unpartnered library schema its own distinct namespace prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: Distinct prefixes put each unpartnered library in its own namespace, which is required for unpartnered schemas.

name: prefixed-group-with-mismatched-partners
description: The partnered-combination rules apply inside each prefixed merge group, not only to unprefixed schemas.
explanation: Schemas sharing the sc: prefix form one merge group and must satisfy the same combination rules as unprefixed schemas. testconflict_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.5.0 while testminimal_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.4.0, so the sc: group has conflicting partners and the load fails even though the unprefixed group (8.5.0) is fine.
common_causes: Assuming prefixed schemas are exempt from partner compatibility rules
Grouping unrelated libraries under one prefix for convenience
correction_strategy: Within each prefix, use library versions sharing one withStandard partner, or split the incompatible libraries into different prefixes.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.0.0 and testminimal_2.1.0 are both partnered with 8.5.0, so the sc: group merges.
Splitting the libraries into different prefixes makes each its own merge group, so the partners no longer need to match.

name: nonexistent-schema-version-in-group
description: A schema version that does not exist cannot be loaded.
explanation: Every entry in the schema specification must name a schema version that the tools can retrieve. testconflict_99.0.0 is a syntactically valid version of a real library, but no such version exists, so the schema cannot be found and the load fails. Because the file was never obtained, no combination rule is being judged: as Appendix B notes, a validator may report this through a file error (FILE_NOT_FOUND in the Python tools) rather than as SCHEMA_LOAD_FAILED.
common_causes: Typo in the version number or library name
Referencing a prerelease or unreleased schema version
Guessing at a version instead of checking the available versions
correction_strategy: Check the available versions of the library and use an exact existing version string.

correction_examples.explanation: testconflict_2.0.0 is an existing version partnered with 8.5.0; testconflict_99.0.0 does not exist.

name: duplicate-schema-in-merge-group
description: The same schema (same name and version) listed twice in one merge group loads; the duplicate is ignored.
explanation: Listing testconflict_2.0.0 twice in the unprefixed merge group is not an error: duplicate schemas (the same name and version) in a merge group are ignored on loading, so the result is the same as listing testconflict_2.0.0 once. Different versions of the same schema, by contrast, cannot appear in the same merge group.
common_causes: Copy-paste duplication in the version specification
Concatenating version lists that share a schema
correction_strategy: No correction is required; the duplicate entry is ignored. Removing it keeps the version specification tidy.

correction_examples.explanation: Both lists load the same vocabulary; the single entry is preferred because the duplicate adds nothing.

name: element-conflict-attribute-value
description: Library schemas sharing an element must give it identical attribute values.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group may share an element only if the element is identical in every schema that declares it. Both libraries declare the top-level tag Attribute-item, but testconflict gives it suggestedTag=Object-one while testclash gives it suggestedTag=Clash-one. The attribute values differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Two libraries reusing a tag name for different purposes
Copies of a shared element drifting apart as the libraries evolve
Updating an attribute value in one library but not in its counterpart
correction_strategy: Make the shared element identical in every library (including attribute values), rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_1.0.0's only shared element (Shared-item) is an identical copy of testconflict's, so the libraries merge.
In separate namespaces the two Attribute-item declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: element-conflict-order-independent
description: An element conflict between two libraries fails the merge whichever library is listed first; schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group can be combined in any order, so this is the same merge group as element-conflict-attribute-value with the two libraries swapped. Both declare the top-level tag Attribute-item with different suggestedTag values (Clash-one versus Object-one). The conflict exists regardless of which library is listed first, so the load fails. Which element a validator reports first may depend on the order, but whether the load fails does not.
common_causes: Expecting the first-listed library to take precedence over a later one for a shared element
Reordering a version list in an attempt to resolve an element conflict
correction_strategy: Make the shared element identical in every library, rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces. Reordering the list does not help.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_1.0.0's only shared element (Shared-item) is an identical copy of testconflict's, so the libraries merge in either order.
In separate namespaces the two Attribute-item declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: element-conflict-description
description: Library schemas sharing an element must give it the same description.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group may share an element only if the element is identical in every schema that declares it, including its description text. Both libraries declare the top-level tag Description-item with the same attributes and position, but the description texts differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Rewording a shared element's description in one library only
Two libraries independently defining the same tag name with different meanings
correction_strategy: Make the shared element's description identical in every library, rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_1.0.0's only shared element (Shared-item) is an identical copy, description included, so the libraries merge.
In separate namespaces the two Description-item declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: element-conflict-ancestor-path
description: Library schemas sharing an element must place it at the same position in the hierarchy.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group may share an element only if the element has the same ancestor path in every schema that declares it. testconflict declares Nested-item as a child of Anchor-item while testclash_4.0.0 declares Nested-item at the top level. The ancestor paths differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Moving a tag to a new parent in one library but not in its counterpart
Two libraries placing the same tag name at different points in their hierarchies
correction_strategy: Place the shared element at the same position in every library, rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_1.0.0's only shared element (Shared-item) sits at the same top-level position in both libraries, so they merge.
In separate namespaces the two Nested-item declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: element-conflict-placeholder-child
description: A shared element must have a placeholder (#) child in all schemas that declare it or in none.
explanation: Schemas in a merge group may share an element only if the element takes a value in every schema that declares it or in none. testconflict's Placeholder-item has a # (takesValue) child while testclash_5.0.0's Placeholder-item has no children. The placeholder presence differs, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Adding a value placeholder to a shared tag in one library only
Two libraries disagreeing on whether a tag takes a value
correction_strategy: Give the shared element the same placeholder child in every library (or none), rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_1.0.0's only shared element (Shared-item) has no placeholder child in either library, so they merge.
In separate namespaces the two Placeholder-item declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: shared-element-compatible-across-libraries
description: Two libraries may declare the same element when the declarations are identical.
explanation: This combination loads. Both libraries declare the top-level tag Shared-item with the same description, the same attributes, the same position, and no placeholder child. Identical shared elements are compatible, so the merge keeps a single copy of Shared-item and the load succeeds.
common_causes: Believing that any tag name overlap between libraries prevents merging
correction_strategy: No correction needed; libraries may share elements as long as the shared declarations are identical.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_3.0.0's shared element differs in description and cannot merge; testclash_1.0.0's shared element is an identical copy and can.

name: same-library-two-incompatible-versions
description: Two versions of the same library cannot appear in one merge group, even when they differ only by a patch-level change such as a revised element description.
explanation: Different versions of the same schema cannot appear in the same merge group, and two versions of one library are never compared element by element. testconflict_2.1.1 is testconflict_2.1.0 with one revised tag description, so the two versions differ only by a patch-level change - yet the load still fails, because the version rule alone bars them. A validator must not merge two versions of one library just because their differences are minor; how similar the versions are is irrelevant.
common_causes: Assuming any two versions of one library can be combined
Expecting a patch release to merge with its predecessor because almost nothing changed
correction_strategy: Use a single version of the library, or give the second version its own namespace so each version is in its own merge group.

correction_examples.explanation: Using one version avoids the version rule entirely.
With its own namespace the patch release is in a separate merge group, and the version rule applies only within a merge group.

name: element-conflict-rooted-vs-top-level
description: A tag rooted in the standard schema in one library cannot merge with an unrooted top-level tag of the same name in another.
explanation: testconflict declares Rooted-tag with rooted=Event, so in the merged vocabulary it sits under the standard Event tag (path Event/Rooted-tag). testclash_6.0.0 declares Rooted-tag as an ordinary top-level tag (path Rooted-tag). The same element cannot be rooted in one library and unrooted in the other: the ancestor paths (and the rooted attribute itself) differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Adding the rooted attribute to a shared tag in one library only
Two libraries disagreeing on whether a subtree extends the standard schema or stands alone
correction_strategy: Give the shared element the same rooted attribute (or none) in every library, rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_8.0.0 declares Rooted-tag with the same rooted=Event anchor as testconflict, so the shared element is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two Rooted-tag declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: element-conflict-rooted-different-anchors
description: A shared rooted tag must be rooted at the same standard schema node in every library.
explanation: testconflict declares Rooted-tag with rooted=Event (merged path Event/Rooted-tag) while testclash_7.0.0 declares Rooted-tag with rooted=Item (merged path Item/Rooted-tag). The two declarations anchor the same tag at different standard schema nodes, so the ancestor paths differ, the elements are incompatible, and the load fails.
common_causes: Re-anchoring a rooted subtree in one library but not in its counterpart
Two libraries extending different standard subtrees with the same tag name
correction_strategy: Root the shared element at the same standard schema node in every library, rename one of the elements, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_8.0.0 roots Rooted-tag at Event, matching testconflict, so the shared element is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two Rooted-tag declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: shared-rooted-hierarchy-different-children
description: A shared element may have different non-placeholder children in different libraries.
explanation: This combination loads. Both libraries declare Rooted-tag identically (rooted=Event, same description) and both declare its child Rooted-one identically. testconflict additionally gives Rooted-tag the child Rooted-two and gives Rooted-one the child Deep-one, while testclash_8.0.0 additionally gives Rooted-tag the child Rooted-three. Different non-placeholder children are allowed for a shared element, so the merged vocabulary has Rooted-tag with children Rooted-one (with Deep-one), Rooted-two, and Rooted-three.
common_causes: Believing two libraries extending the same shared subtree cannot be combined
correction_strategy: No correction needed; libraries may each add their own children under a shared element as long as the shared elements themselves are identical.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_9.0.0 changes the shared child Rooted-one's description and cannot merge; testclash_8.0.0 keeps the shared elements identical and adds only its own child.

name: element-conflict-in-shared-child
description: A changed shared child makes libraries incompatible even when their non-shared siblings would be allowed.
explanation: Both libraries declare Rooted-tag identically, and testclash_9.0.0's own child Rooted-three would be an allowed non-shared addition. But both libraries also declare the child Rooted-one, and testclash_9.0.0 gives it a different description. The compatibility rules apply to every shared element, not just the top of a shared subtree, so the changed shared child makes the libraries incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Rewording a shared child's description while adding library-specific siblings
Assuming only the root of a shared subtree needs to match
correction_strategy: Make every shared element of the subtree identical across the libraries, rename the changed child, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_8.0.0 declares the shared child Rooted-one identically and keeps its own sibling Rooted-three, so the libraries merge.
In separate namespaces the two Rooted-one declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: shared-rooted-tag-disjoint-children
description: A shared element's children may be entirely disjoint between libraries.
explanation: This combination loads. Both libraries declare Rooted-tag identically (rooted=Event, same description), but their child sets do not overlap at all: testconflict declares Rooted-one (with Deep-one) and Rooted-two, while testclash_10.0.0 declares only Rooted-four. A shared element's children may be entirely disjoint, so the merged Rooted-tag carries all four children and the load succeeds.
common_causes: Believing a shared element must have the same children everywhere it is declared
correction_strategy: No correction needed; only the shared elements themselves must match, and child sets may be disjoint.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_6.0.0's Rooted-tag is unrooted and conflicts; testclash_10.0.0's Rooted-tag matches testconflict's and only its children differ, which is allowed.

name: shared-hierarchy-diverges-at-grandchild
description: Libraries sharing an identical chain of elements may diverge below it.
explanation: This combination loads. Both libraries declare the chain Rooted-tag (rooted=Event) with child Rooted-one identically. Below that chain they diverge: testconflict gives Rooted-one the child Deep-one while testclash_11.0.0 gives it the child Deep-two. Because every shared element is identical and the differing grandchildren are not shared, the merge succeeds and Rooted-one carries both Deep-one and Deep-two.
common_causes: Believing hierarchies that overlap for several levels cannot be combined
correction_strategy: No correction needed; libraries may extend a shared chain with different elements at any depth as long as the shared elements match.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_12.0.0 changes the shared grandchild Deep-one's description and cannot merge; testclash_11.0.0 adds its own grandchild Deep-two instead, which is allowed.

name: element-conflict-in-shared-grandchild
description: The element compatibility rules recurse into every depth of a shared hierarchy.
explanation: Both libraries declare the chain Rooted-tag (rooted=Event) with child Rooted-one identically, and both declare the grandchild Deep-one under Rooted-one. testclash_12.0.0 gives Deep-one a different description. Compatibility applies to every shared element at every depth, so the changed shared grandchild makes the libraries incompatible and the load fails, even though everything above it matches.
common_causes: Rewording a deeply nested shared element's description in one library only
Assuming compatibility is only checked near the top of a shared subtree
correction_strategy: Make the shared element identical at every depth of the shared hierarchy, rename the changed element, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_11.0.0 leaves the shared chain identical and adds its own grandchild Deep-two instead of changing the shared Deep-one.
In separate namespaces the two Deep-one declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: aux-new-unit-class-merges-directly
description: New library schema auxiliary elements (unit classes with their units, unit modifiers, value classes, and schema attributes) are merged directly into the group vocabulary.
explanation: This combination loads. testconflict_2.0.0 and testaux_1.0.0 are both partnered with standard schema 8.5.0, and no auxiliary element of testaux appears in testconflict or in the standard partner: the unit class auxUnits (with its units auxunit and bigauxunit), the unit modifier auxMod, the value class auxClass, and the schema attribute auxAttribute are all new. New library schema unit classes and their accompanying units are merged directly, as are new value classes, unit modifiers, and schema attributes, so the merged vocabulary validates Aux-measure values with auxUnits units and Aux-value values against auxClass.
common_causes: Believing library schemas cannot add unit classes, value classes, unit modifiers, or schema attributes to a merge group
Believing auxiliary sections must be identical across the schemas of a merge group
correction_strategy: No correction needed; an auxiliary element that appears in only one schema of a merge group is merged directly.

correction_examples.explanation: testaux_1.0.0 is partnered with 8.5.0, so it cannot share a merge group with standard schema 8.4.0; with testconflict_2.0.0 (also partnered with 8.5.0) the libraries merge and testaux's auxiliary elements are added directly.

name: aux-identical-elements-compatible
description: Two libraries may declare the same auxiliary elements when the declarations are identical.
explanation: This combination loads. testclash_13.0.0 declares identical copies of every testaux_1.0.0 auxiliary element: the unit class auxUnits with its units auxunit and bigauxunit, the unit modifier auxMod, the value class auxClass, and the schema attribute auxAttribute, each with the same attribute values, properties, and description. The element compatibility rules apply to auxiliary elements exactly as to tags, so the identical shared elements merge into single copies and the load succeeds.
common_causes: Believing that any overlap in the auxiliary sections of two libraries prevents merging
correction_strategy: No correction needed; libraries may share auxiliary elements as long as the shared declarations are identical.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_14.0.0 changes the conversionFactor of the shared unit auxunit and cannot merge; testclash_13.0.0's auxiliary elements are identical copies and can.

name: aux-unit-attribute-conflict
description: Library schemas sharing a unit must give it identical attribute values.
explanation: The element compatibility rules apply to units as they do to tags. Both libraries declare the unit class auxUnits with the units auxunit and bigauxunit, but testaux gives auxunit conversionFactor=1.0 while testclash_14.0.0 gives it conversionFactor=2.0. The attribute values of the shared unit differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Correcting a unit's conversion factor in one library but not in its counterpart
Two libraries reusing a unit name with different meanings
correction_strategy: Make the shared unit identical in every library (attribute values included), rename one of the units, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_13.0.0 declares auxunit with the same conversionFactor as testaux, so the shared unit is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two auxunit declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: aux-new-units-under-shared-class
description: A library may add new units under a shared unit class when the shared units themselves are identical.
explanation: This combination loads. Both libraries declare the unit class auxUnits identically, with identical copies of the units auxunit and bigauxunit. testclash_15.0.0 additionally declares the unit smallauxunit, which testaux does not have. New library schema units under an existing unit class are merged if there are no conflicts, so the merged auxUnits carries all three units and Aux-measure values can use any of them.
common_causes: Believing a shared unit class must have exactly the same units in every library that declares it
correction_strategy: No correction needed; a library may add its own units under a shared unit class as long as the units the libraries share are identical.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_14.0.0 changes a shared unit's conversionFactor and cannot merge; testclash_15.0.0 keeps the shared units identical and only adds its own unit smallauxunit, which is allowed.

name: aux-value-class-conflict
description: Library schemas sharing a value class must give it identical attribute values.
explanation: The element compatibility rules apply to value classes as they do to tags. Both libraries declare the value class auxClass, but testaux gives it allowedCharacter=letters while testclash_16.0.0 gives it allowedCharacter=digits. The attribute values of the shared value class differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Changing the allowed characters of a shared value class in one library only
Two libraries reusing a value class name for different value formats
correction_strategy: Make the shared value class identical in every library, rename one of the value classes, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_13.0.0 declares auxClass with the same allowedCharacter value as testaux, so the shared value class is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two auxClass declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: aux-schema-attribute-property-conflict
description: Library schemas sharing a schema attribute must give it the same properties.
explanation: For schema attribute elements, the properties are the attribute values that are compared: two schema attributes with the same name must have the same properties. testaux declares auxAttribute with boolRange while testclash_17.0.0 declares auxAttribute with no properties at all (a string-valued attribute). The properties differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Dropping or adding a property of a shared schema attribute in one library only
Two libraries disagreeing on whether an attribute is boolean or takes a value
correction_strategy: Give the shared schema attribute the same properties in every library, rename one of the attributes, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_13.0.0 declares auxAttribute with the same boolRange as testaux, so the shared schema attribute is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two auxAttribute declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: aux-schema-attribute-description-conflict
description: Library schemas sharing a schema attribute must give it the same description.
explanation: The element compatibility rules include the description text, for auxiliary elements as for tags. Both libraries declare the schema attribute auxAttribute with the same boolRange, but the description texts differ. The shared element is therefore incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Rewording a shared schema attribute's description in one library only
Two libraries independently defining the same attribute name with different meanings
correction_strategy: Make the shared schema attribute's description identical in every library, rename one of the attributes, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_13.0.0's auxAttribute is an identical copy, description included, so the libraries merge.
In separate namespaces the two auxAttribute declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: aux-unit-modifier-conflict
description: Library schemas sharing a unit modifier must give it identical attribute values.
explanation: The element compatibility rules apply to unit modifiers as they do to tags. Both libraries declare the unit modifier auxMod with SIUnitModifier, but testaux gives it conversionFactor=100.0 while testclash_19.0.0 gives it conversionFactor=10.0. The attribute values of the shared unit modifier differ, so the elements are incompatible and the load fails.
common_causes: Correcting a unit modifier's conversion factor in one library but not in its counterpart
Two libraries reusing a unit modifier name with different scale factors
correction_strategy: Make the shared unit modifier identical in every library, rename one of the modifiers, or load the libraries in separate namespaces.

correction_examples.explanation: testclash_13.0.0 declares auxMod with the same conversionFactor as testaux, so the shared unit modifier is compatible.
In separate namespaces the two auxMod declarations never meet, so no compatibility check applies.

name: conflicting-libraries-in-separate-namespaces
description: A library pair that fails to merge loads once one member is given its own namespace prefix.
explanation: This combination loads. Unprefixed, testconflict_2.0.0 and testclash_2.0.0 fail to merge because both declare the tag Attribute-item with different suggestedTag values (see element-conflict-attribute-value). With the cl: prefix, testclash_2.0.0 forms its own merge group, each group resolves independently with its own copy of the 8.5.0 partner, and the two Attribute-item declarations never meet. Both tags are then usable: Attribute-item refers to the testconflict tag and cl:Attribute-item to the testclash tag.
common_causes: Believing two libraries with conflicting elements can never be used together
Omitting the namespace prefix that keeps incompatible libraries apart
correction_strategy: No correction needed; put one member of an incompatible library pair in its own namespace and prefix its tags in annotations.

correction_examples.explanation: Unprefixed, the conflicting Attribute-item declarations share one merge group and fail; the prefix puts testclash_2.0.0 in its own merge group.

name: same-library-two-versions-in-separate-namespaces
description: Two versions of one library load together when each version has its own namespace.
explanation: This combination loads. Two versions of one library cannot share a merge group (see same-library-two-versions-in-group), but with the alt: prefix testconflict_2.1.1 forms its own merge group. Each group resolves independently with its own copy of the 8.5.0 partner, so neither the version rule nor the element comparison ever applies across the groups, and both versions' tags are usable with the appropriate prefix.
common_causes: Believing two versions of one library can never appear in the same version specification
Omitting the namespace prefix the second version requires
correction_strategy: No correction needed; give the second version of the library its own namespace prefix and prefix its tags in annotations.

correction_examples.explanation: Unprefixed, two versions of one library share a merge group and fail; the prefix puts the second version in its own merge group.
